newsitem.title: UK: BA disappointed on catering staff ballot.
newsitem.headline: BA disappointed on catering staff ballot.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on late on Wednesday it was disappointed staff had voted to reject the terms of a company proposal to sell its Heathrow airport catering unit.
It added union representatives had asked for further talks on the terms since the deal was rejected earlier on Wednesday.

"Since the ballot was counted this morning, the union representatives have gone to see BA catering management to explain they don't want to go on strike and that they want further clarification on the deal they have voted on," BA spokesman Iain Burns told Reuters.

The threat of industrial action from the catering staff comes on the second day of a three-day strike by cabin crew over newly-imposed pay structures and conditions which has grounded hundreds of BA flights.
BA said in a statement that deal they had offered the catering employees was extremely generous.

"Employees have told managers that a major concern had been staff travel," BA said. "The British Airways proposal has offered continuation of existing staff travel benefits. In addition, the package secured jobs and current terms and conditions, including pension entitlements."
BA said discussions with several interested parties on the sale of the business were well advanced and the airline remained committed to ensuring the best possible deal for the future of its staff.
